name: Manas Gumbez
full: Manas Gumbez (mausoleum in the Manas Ordo historical and cultural complex)
near: Tash-Aryk — ~1 km (OSM); the village has guesthouses, shops and cafés (too.kg). The town of Talas is 13–15 km to the west (Nomad's Land, too.kg; kyrgyzstan-tourism.com gives 22 km).
short: A 14th-century brick mausoleum (around 1334) near Tash-Aryk village outside Talas — the main monument of the Manas Ordo complex, linked to the epic about the hero Manas; after a two-year reconstruction the complex reopened on 11.09.2026.
desc: Manas Gumbez is a medieval mausoleum of fired brick with carved clay cladding, Karakhanid ornaments and an Arabic inscription; it dates from the 14th century, around 1334 (Nomad's Land, 2GIS). According to the inscription the tomb belonged to the daughter of a ruler of the Chagatai ulus (Kenizek Khatun), but popular tradition regards it as the grave of Manas: allegedly the hero's wife Kanykey ordered a woman's name to be written so that enemies would not desecrate the burial (Nomad's Land). In Soviet times the Manas Ordo complex (about 225 ha) was created around the mausoleum: an epic museum, a lapidarium with petroglyphs, balbals and stones with Yenisei runic writing, an avenue of sculptures of the epic's heroes, a yurt for performances of the epic by manaschi (epic reciters), and Karool-Debe hill with a view of the valley (too.kg; visitsilkroad.org; economist.kg). From 01.08.2025 the complex was closed for its first reconstruction in 30 years (24.kg); on 11.09.2026 the president opened the renovated Manas Ordo: a new congress hall, an administrative building, a pilgrims' house, and the museum expanded from 700 to 1,090 m²; the cost of the work was 1.4 billion som (economist.kg, for.kg).
guide: The main intrigue of the Gumbez is the inscription: the wall says that the daughter of a Chagatai emir is buried here, while legend insists this is a ruse by Kanykey, who hid Manas's grave from his enemies. Take a close look at the carved terracotta of the facade — it is one of the best examples of medieval brick architecture in the country. After the mausoleum, look into the renovated epic museum and the lapidarium with balbals and runic stones, and then climb Karool-Debe hill — from there you can see the whole Talas Valley. The complex has only just reopened after reconstruction, so check opening hours and ticket prices by phone or in Talas before you go.
see: The Manas Gumbez mausoleum (14th century) with carved terracotta and an inscription; the renovated Manas epic museum (1,090 m²); the lapidarium — petroglyphs, stone tools, balbals, 13 stones with Yenisei runic writing; an avenue of sculptures of the epic's heroes; a yurt for performances of the epic; Karool-Debe hill with a view of the valley; Saka and Wusun burial mounds (too.kg; visitsilkroad.org; economist.kg 2026).
skip: You aren't interested in history and the epic — there is not much natural scenery here, it is above all a memorial. You aren't going to the Talas region — from Bishkek it is 5–6 hours one way.
diff: Easy: a paved road to the complex, a walk through the park; the climb up Karool-Debe is a short walk (editorial).
when: April–October; the complex operates year-round (before the reconstruction). On national holidays and event days (the congress hall, Independence Day on 31 August) restrictions and crowds are possible (editorial).
hours: The complex reopened after reconstruction on 11.09.2026 (economist.kg, for.kg). On Google Maps as of 03.10.2026 it still showed “temporarily closed” — probably not updated. Opening hours after the reopening have not been published — check before you go.
daytime: Morning or the second half of the day: soft light on the brickwork and views from Karool-Debe; in summer it is hot in the Talas Valley by day (editorial).
how: From Bishkek to Talas: marshrutkas (minibuses) from the Ak-Kula hippodrome in western Bishkek (the Western bus station has been closed since 10.2024) (~350 som, 5.5–6 h) or a shared taxi from ~650 som/seat (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com; Wikivoyage — data up to 2025), via the Otmok Pass. From Talas — 15 km east to Tash-Aryk on a good paved road; taxis and marshrutkas run daily from Talas bus station/bazaar (visitsilkroad.org; Wikivoyage — 20 som, an outdated price). By your own car: Bishkek — Sosnovka — Too-Ashuu tunnel — Suusamyr — Otmok Pass — Talas (~300 km); at the Sosnovka post a fee for the Bishkek — Osh highway tunnels is charged: 50 som (Kyrgyz plates) / 200 som (foreign), since 01.01.2024.
needcar: Yes: to Talas and from Talas to the complex (marshrutka, taxi). On site — on foot.
self: Yes: the complex is accessible without a guide; museum tours are with the complex's guide (digital equipment for tours was installed during the reconstruction, economist.kg).
roadtype: Paved: a good road from Talas to the complex (too.kg); Bishkek — Talas — paved through the Too-Ashuu and Otmok passes.
traveltime: Bishkek — Talas ~5.5–6 h (marshrutka); Talas — Manas Ordo ~20 min by car (15 km, estimate).
stay: Guesthouses in Tash-Aryk (too.kg; names not found); in Talas — guesthouses $10–30/night, 2–3* hotels from $30 (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com); Hotel Talant — 300–400 som/person (Wikivoyage, an outdated price). A pilgrims' house and guest houses have been built on the complex's grounds (24.kg, economist.kg) — the arrangements for accommodating tourists are not confirmed.
net: There is mobile coverage (visitsilkroad.org); operators not specified.
entry: Not confirmed after the reconstruction (reopened 11.09.2026). Before the reconstruction: foreigners 200 som, Kyrgyz citizens 30 som (Wikivoyage, data up to 2025). The new rate for the Manas Ordo complex has not been published in official announcements — check on site.
transfer: GoBus Bishkek — Talas 500 som (06.2025, via Kazakhstan); marshrutka Bishkek — Talas ~350 som; shared taxi from ~650 som/seat (kyrgyzstan-tourism.com, year not given); Talas — Manas Ordo — marshrutka 20 som (Wikivoyage up to 2025, outdated), taxi — by arrangement.
bring: A hat and water (open area, hot in summer), modest clothing for visiting the mausoleum (a holy place for pilgrims), cash for tickets.
warn: The complex reopened after reconstruction on 11.09.2026, but opening hours and rates after the reopening have not been published; on Google Maps (03.10.2026) it still shows “temporarily closed” — call ahead. This is a place of pilgrimage — behave respectfully and dress modestly. During state events access may be restricted.
food: Talas beans are the valley's main product; beshbarmak and boorsoki in the cafés of Tash-Aryk and Talas (typical of the region; specific eateries have not been verified).
reviews: Google Maps: 4.8 from 867 ratings (listed as “Kumbez Manasa”, catalogue check 10.2026). 2GIS: 3.3 from 21 ratings (07.10.2026). Pros — history, the museum, the atmosphere; cons in older reviews — the condition of the complex before the reconstruction (per 2GIS, details not disclosed).
p.sum: The Manas Ordo complex with the Manas Gumbez reopened after reconstruction on 12.09.2026 (a new 1,500 m² museum, cottages, canteens); it is 12–15 km east of Talas by the village of Tash-Aryk — city marshrutkas and taxis go there. Base yourself in Talas: from Bishkek take a marshrutka/shared taxi via Otmok (5.5–6 h) or GoBus via Kazakhstan. The rate and hours after the reopening have not been published — check on site; dress modestly.

p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Bishkek — Talas via Otmok. Day 2: morning — Manas Ordo, afternoon — Besh-Tash National Park (lower gorge). Day 3: Lake Besh-Tash (12 km round trip from the camp) or the Kirov Reservoir on the way to Taraz/Bishkek via Kazakhstan.
p.season: April–October — comfortable; 31 August and epic festivals — mass events, crowds. In winter the complex is open (not confirmed), the road over Otmok is icy.
p.budget.economy: ~1,500–2,500 som/person per day: marshrutka Bishkek — Talas ~350–500 som, local marshrutka, guesthouse $10–30, entry (2026 rate not published).
p.budget.comfort: A car with a driver from Bishkek for 2 days + a hotel from $30/person.
p.permits: Not needed. Complex ticket — the post-reconstruction rate has not been published. If travelling via Kazakhstan, you need the entry regime for Kazakhstan.
p.access: The new landscaped complex — the paths suit older people and probably wheelchairs (not confirmed). With kids — yes. With dogs to the holy place — not recommended.
